exposure: Small head circumference plus abdominal circumference <= p10 (SHC+)
Small head circumference plus abdominal circumference <= p10 and Doppler abnormalities (SHC+D)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies where the fetus had a head circumference between -3.0 SD and -1.64 SD on expert ultrasound examination between 18 and 24 weeks of gestational age.
finding: Fetuses with isolated small head circumference (ISHC) and small head circumference plus abdominal circumference (SHC+) had high survival rates (96%), while those with additional Doppler abnormalities (SHC+D) had significantly lower survival (38%).
mod_finding: Less fetuses in the SHC+ subgroup were delivered vaginally (61%) compared to the ISHC subgroup (73%).
followup_time: Postnatally, through the neonatal period and beyond for diagnosis of congenital and genetic anomalies.
gest_age: Fetal head circumference was measured between 18 and 24 weeks of gestational age for cohort inclusion; gestational age at birth is not specified.
